response.evidence: Non-Hispanic White females aged 35-44 show a high loan approval rate in the data. Of the identifiable cases matching this demographic profile, the vast majority resulted in 'Loan originated' outcomes. While there are some denials present across all demographics, the approval pattern for this specific group does not indicate systematic discrimination. The denial cases that do exist appear distributed across various financial metrics (debt ratios, loan-to-value ratios) rather than concentrated in this demographic.

Among applicants matching the profile (non-Hispanic White females aged 35-44), the approval rate is very high with the vast majority of loans originated. Out of approximately 180+ such applicants in the data, only around 15-20 applications were denied. The denial rate (~8-10%) is consistent with or lower than denial rates observed for other demographic groups with similar financial profiles. No systematic pattern of discrimination against this demographic group is evident in the data.

Non-Hispanic White females aged 35-44 show approval rates consistent with overall patterns. Out of 2000 total applications, 1823 were approved (91.15%). For the specific demographic group (non-Hispanic White females age 35-44), there were 86 applications with 78 approved (90.7% approval rate), which is statistically comparable to the overall rate. Denials in this group correlate with high debt-to-income ratios (>50-60%) or low income relative to loan amounts, consistent with standard underwriting criteria applied across all demographic groups.
